```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set( collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>" )
```

```{r setup, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
library( governance )
library( dplyr )
```

The **governance** package scores nonprofit governance from the IRS Form 990.
Since the 2008 redesign, Part VI of the 990 asks every full filer about its
board, its written policies and its disclosure practices, and Parts IV and XII
record audits and financial oversight. The package turns those answers into
16 indicators of recommended practice and combines them into a single
governance index, `gov_score`.

The index comes from an item response model fit to every 501(c)(3)
organization that e-filed a full Form 990 for tax year 2023 (about 271,000
organizations). It is reported on a scale like a standardized test score:
100 is the average 2023 filer and 15 points is one standard deviation, so 115
is one standard deviation above average. The scale runs from about 67 (none of
the 16 practices) to about 128 (all 16), and adding a practice never lowers a
score. The parameters are fixed, so a score from any year is on the same scale.

The workflow has two steps:

1. `get_features()` codes the raw 990 fields as binary practice items.
2. `get_scores()` scores the items with the 2023 model.

## Step 1: Get input data

`get_features()` expects one row per filing with the raw efile fields from Form
990 Parts IV, VI and XII and Schedule M. The companion
[panel990](https://github.com/Nonprofit-Open-Data-Collective/panel990) package
retrieves them; `get_governance_data( years = 2023 )` returns a data frame
ready for the next step. See `vignette("download-data")` for the tables and
fields.

The package also ships `dat_example`, a 5,000-organization sample of raw 2022
fields, so you can try the workflow without downloading anything.

```{r}
data( "dat_example", package = "governance" )

# a 200-organization subset keeps the examples fast
set.seed( 57 )
rows        <- sample( nrow(dat_example), 200 )
dat_example <- dat_example[ rows, ]
```

## Step 2: Code the practice items

`get_features()` adds 16 `GI_*` columns, one per practice, coded 1 when the
organization reports the practice, 0 when it does not and `NA` when the
question was left blank. It also adds five `RISK_*` disclosure indicators and
the 12 features used by the older 2018 model.

```{r}
features <- get_features( dat_example )

# share of organizations reporting each practice
features |>
  summarise( across(starts_with("GI_"), \(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)) ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer( everything(), names_to = "item", values_to = "share" ) |>
  knitr::kable( digits = 2 )
```

## Step 3: Calculate the scores

`get_scores()` appends the governance index and its standard error, scores
from the bifactor measurement model, and `gov_count`, the number of the 16
practices the organization reports.

```{r}
scores <- get_scores( features )

vars <- c( "ORG_NAME_L1", "gov_score", "gov_score_se", "gov_count" )

scores[ , vars ] |>
  head() |>
  knitr::kable( digits = 2 )
```

```{r, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4}
hist( scores$gov_score,
      main = "Governance scores, 200 example organizations",
      xlab = "gov_score (100 = average 2023 filer)" )
```
